newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - June 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - June 2.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) step up security at their massive "one-four" base in the northern Wanni region where LTTE leader Velupillai Prabhakaran is believed to be operating from, as security forces push deeper into the Wanni.
President Chandrika Kumaratunga says government plans to launch educational reforms from next month, with proper job orientation and in keeping with modern day technology developments and needs.
Government plans to present before the people its political solution to the country's ethnic war by November, Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte says.
Sri Lankan troops, on a major offensive against the LTTE, capture huge stockpile of food in northern Wanni region.

Government to buy dried chillies from farmers at 70 rupees per kg, despite cheaper imported chillies being available in the market, the state buying arm the Cooperative Wholesale Establishment says. Farmers in the island's dry zone earlier burnt some of their chilli harvest, protesting a government decision to allow private traders to import chillies from India.
Police arrest 14 employees of Airlanka and the Department of Immigration and Emigration for allegedly being involved in a ring to smuggle Sri Lankans abroad on forged papers.
